notebooks.title: Revised AI Dependency and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
notebooks.summary: Empirical survey data from athletes reveals a serial association model linking AI training recommendation dependence to body signal outsourcing, reduced self-regulation, training decision hesitation, and diminished self-efficacy.
notebooks.findings: AI training recommendation dependence is positively associated with body signal outsourcing and a reduced sense of self-regulation among athletes. [source-d9addfec171d4b5d]
notebooks.limitations: The findings are based on cross-sectional questionnaire data from 381 athletes, which limits causal inference and requires longitudinal validation.
notebooks.next_questions: How do these serial association pathways vary across different types of skill-dominant versus physical-dominant sports over extended training cycles?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook findings with new empirical sources detailing AI dependency pathways in athletes.

review.alternative: Athletes who already experience lower self-regulation might independently seek out AI recommendations rather than AI usage causing the outsourcing.
review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal panel data showing that baseline self-regulation levels do not predict subsequent AI adoption.

notebooks.title: Limitations of Automated Epistemic Self-Correction
notebooks.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in automated hypothesis testing and system falsification, these systems operate within fixed methodological parameters. They do not demonstrate autonomous revision of their foundational epistemic assumptions, which remain subject to the external normative constraints identified in ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2].
notebooks.findings:
Automated falsification agents like Popper can achieve performance comparable to human scientists in validating specific biological hypotheses. [source-0c3114b8bfe140df]

Bayesian Optimization enhances falsification efficiency in Cyber-Physical Systems, but relies on predefined system specifications. [source-f0f5479363014d20]
notebooks.limitations: Existing automated frameworks are highly efficient at testing defined hypotheses but currently lack mechanisms to reflectively challenge their own underlying logic, definitions, or procedural frameworks without external intervention.
notebooks.next_questions: Can meta-level auditing frameworks be integrated with operational falsification agents to create a hierarchical self-correcting system?
notebooks.reason: Revision based on new findings regarding Popper and Bayesian Optimization as specific falsification mechanisms distinct from broad epistemic self-correction.

detail.statement: Current automated meta-reasoning frameworks operate strictly within fixed methodological parameters and lack the reflexive capacity to autonomously revise their foundational epistemic assumptions or procedural definitions without external intervention.
detail.reason: Synthesis of current project evidence shows that agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] excel at falsification within defined bounds, while ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2] highlights the continued necessity for external governance to ensure normative consistency.

detail.question: What are the theoretical and architectural requirements for a computational system to transition from episodic memory storage to the instantiation of a persistent personal identity?
detail.next_step: Synthesize existing philosophical and computational theories of selfhood to establish a baseline for identifying 'persistent identity' vs 'memory retention'.

detail.title: Limitations of Automated Epistemic Self-Correction
detail.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in automated hypothesis testing and system falsification, these systems operate within fixed methodological parameters. They do not demonstrate autonomous revision of their foundational epistemic assumptions, which remain subject to the external normative constraints identified in ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2].
detail.findings:
Automated falsification agents like Popper can achieve performance comparable to human scientists in validating specific biological hypotheses. [source-0c3114b8bfe140df]

Bayesian Optimization enhances falsification efficiency in Cyber-Physical Systems, but relies on predefined system specifications. [source-f0f5479363014d20]
detail.limitations: Existing automated frameworks are highly efficient at testing defined hypotheses but currently lack mechanisms to reflectively challenge their own underlying logic, definitions, or procedural frameworks without external intervention.
detail.next_questions: Can meta-level auditing frameworks be integrated with operational falsification agents to create a hierarchical self-correcting system?
detail.reason: Revision based on new findings regarding Popper and Bayesian Optimization as specific falsification mechanisms distinct from broad epistemic self-correction.

detail.title: Revised AI Dependency and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
detail.summary: Empirical survey data from athletes reveals a serial association model linking AI training recommendation dependence to body signal outsourcing, reduced self-regulation, training decision hesitation, and diminished self-efficacy.
detail.findings: AI training recommendation dependence is positively associated with body signal outsourcing and a reduced sense of self-regulation among athletes. [source-d9addfec171d4b5d]
detail.limitations: The findings are based on cross-sectional questionnaire data from 381 athletes, which limits causal inference and requires longitudinal validation.
detail.next_questions: How do these serial association pathways vary across different types of skill-dominant versus physical-dominant sports over extended training cycles?
detail.reason: Revising notebook findings with new empirical sources detailing AI dependency pathways in athletes.

review.alternative: Athletes who already experience lower self-regulation might independently seek out AI recommendations rather than AI usage causing the outsourcing.
review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal panel data showing that baseline self-regulation levels do not predict subsequent AI adoption.
